title: Small+Large Request Packing — Field Journal
content:
Context and motivation:
I ran a set of informal field experiments to understand how request packing rules interact with a mixed workload: very small requests (single-token-ish responses, ~5–40 tokens generated) interleaved with large chat completions (~800–1500 tokens). Production traces show these patterns when background async agents (embeddings, short prompts) coexist with long-form assistants. The goal was to capture the failure modes that cause large-response starvation and unexpected p95/p99 increases for the large requests when packing aggressively for the small ones.

Environment / setup:
- Cluster: dev-fleet-2 (A100s), single-region (us-west-2).
- Runtime: local branch packer-experiments (kernel selection unchanged).
- Model: open-llama-13b-8k (float16), single replica for baseline, 3-replica pool for throughput runs.
- Load generator: synthetic arrival generator (zipfian mix) with controllable mix ratio, and a thin client that simulates prefill + generation.
- Observability: per-request traces + token-level timestamps, KV cache hit/miss, batch composition logs.
- Measurement windows: 10 minutes warmup + 20 minutes steady-state per run.

Workload definitions:
- Small request: mean response tokens ~18, median latency when isolated ~12ms p50, ~28ms p95 (fast path).
- Large request: mean response tokens ~1000, isolated p50 ~320ms, p95 ~480ms.
- Mix ratio tested: 90% small / 10% large (S90-L10), 70/30, and 50/50.
- Concurrency levels: 50, 150, 400 concurrent in-flight requests.

Packer configurations tested:
A. Conservative (baseline): max-pack-size=64, prefer-same-size=false, pack-window=8ms
B. Aggressive-small-first: max-pack-size=128, prefer-small-requests=true, pack-window=12ms
C. Isolation-hint: max-pack-size=64, reserve-2-slots-for-large=true, pack-window=8ms
D. Dynamic-slab: adaptive packing where packer keeps small-request slab and large slab, window 6–16ms depending on short-term load

Key raw numbers (steady-state summaries):
Scenario: S90-L10, concurrency=150
- A (Conservative): overall qps 520, small p50=14ms p95=30ms p99=68ms, large p50=340ms p95=520ms p99=890ms, pack efficiency (tokens saved vs no packing) ~18%
- B (Aggressive small-first): overall qps 610, small p50=13ms p95=26ms p99=60ms, large p50=420ms p95=760ms p99=1700ms, pack efficiency ~34%
- C (Isolation-hint): overall qps 490, small p50=15ms p95=32ms p99=70ms, large p50=360ms p95=540ms p99=930ms, pack efficiency ~16%
- D (Dynamic-slab): overall qps 570, small p50=13ms p95=28ms p99=72ms, large p50=330ms p95=500ms p99=980ms, pack efficiency ~22%

Scenario: S70-L30, concurrency=400 (stress)
- A: overall qps 1120, small p95=48ms, large p95=930ms, p99 for large frequently > 2s (many evictions observed)
- B: overall qps 1280, small p95=40ms, large p95=1600ms, p99 >> 3s (severe tail)
- C: overall qps 980, large p95=760ms, p99 ~1.3s (far better tail than B)
- D: overall qps 1150, large p95=680ms, p99 ~1.05s

Interesting traces / qualitative observations:
- Sandwich effect: In aggressive packing (B) I saw large requests repeatedly being delayed by multiple consecutive small-pack batches. Packing increases throughput but also increases how often a large request's tokens get split across batches with many pre-empting small batches, causing prefill delays and more frequent KV cache churn.
- Eviction spikes: When concurrency > 300 and mix >= 30% large, memory pressure + packing windows resulted in frequent KV cache evictions for large requests mid-generation, amplifying tail latency by 2–4x. Traces show a tight correlation between pack-window spikes and eviction events.
- Jitter-resonance: Pack-window jitter (variance in when the packer flushes) produced micro-queuing where a large request that arrived just after a flush waited ~pack-window+next-batch-window, compounding via arrival alignment.
- Reservation helps: Isolation-hint (C) with two reserved slots kept a lower p99 for large requests while sacrificing some overall throughput. The effect was most visible at S70-L30.

Quick conclusions (draft):
- Pure throughput optimization via aggressive small-first packing materially hurts long-request tail latency in mixed workloads. Not safe as a default for multi-tenant environments with heterogeneous request sizes.
- A modest static reservation (C) or dynamic-slab (D) that adapts to short-term mix gives a good tradeoff: most throughput gains of B but bounding long-request tail with much lower p99.
- Monitoring signals to detect harmful mixes: rise in eviction-rate, increase in per-request split-count, pack-window occupancy approaching max-pack-size, and long-request prefill delay distribution skew.

Action items / next steps:
- Instrument a metric: large_request_split_ratio (how often a large request is split across bags). Put alert when > 0.25 and aggregate p99_large > 750ms. (TODO: create JIRA ticket).
- Try variant E: small-priority but preempt-once — allow small batches to preempt only once per large generation (simulate fairness). Quick experiment planned week of Jan 8.
- Evaluate packer window smoothing: reduce variance in pack flush timing and measure tail impact.
- Add simulation to the local replay harness reproducing the sandwich arrival alignment to test deterministic cases.

Notes to self / gotchas:
- Observable pack efficiency numbers are noisy; need 95% CI and more repeats. Single 20-minute runs good for signal but not statistically robust.
- Kernel-level changes (attention scheduling) may interact badly with split requests; keep packer changes orthogonal to kernel change for clean attribution.
- Customer anecdote: one enterprise reported elevated assistant tail when embedding pipeline was enabled — likely because the embedding requests are small and frequent. This maps to the S90-L10 pattern here.

Files / artifacts from these runs:
- batch-logs/pack-B-trace-2025-11-10.log (raw per-batch composition)
- traces/large-slow-tail-sample-2025-11-10.json (sampled trace)
- scripts/compare-packers.sh (replay harness recipe)

If anyone reads this and wants to reproduce quickly: grab the branch packer-experiments, start local replay with mix generator config mix=S70-L30, concurrency=400, set packer config to switch between A..D. I left the exact run commands in scripts/README in the same folder.

Signed-off: Marco
